text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
text.es: Busca las notas de la frase 1: cada una te espera hasta que estés en ella.

text.en: The tune began in 1850 as Study No. 23, a choir-practice piece in Richard Storrs Willis's Church Chorals and Choir Studies, set to Philip Doddridge's "See Israel's gentle shepherd stand". It held only about the first half of CAROL, the tune we sing.
text.es: La melodía empezó en 1850 como el Study No. 23, una pieza para el ensayo del coro en Church Chorals and Choir Studies, de Richard Storrs Willis, con la letra de "See Israel's gentle shepherd stand", de Philip Doddridge. Solo tenía más o menos la primera mitad de CAROL, la melodía que cantamos.

source.en: R. Storrs Willis, Church Chorals and Choir Studies (New York: Clark, Austin and Smith, 1850), Study No. 23, p. 93; Princeton Theological Seminary Library copy, read from the scan; Hymnology Archive, "It Came Upon the Midnight Clear"
source.es: R. Storrs Willis, Church Chorals and Choir Studies (Nueva York: Clark, Austin and Smith, 1850), Study No. 23, p. 93; ejemplar de la Princeton Theological Seminary Library, leído en el escaneo; Hymnology Archive, "It Came Upon the Midnight Clear"

text.en: Sing your part with the other parts, and the guide with you. Hold your line while the others move.

text.en: The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
text.es: La guía deja de cantar: tu parte, solo con las demás voces. "Escuchar mi nota" te da tu primera nota, suave.

text.en: Once more on your own, from the top.
text.es: Otra vez sin guía, desde el principio.

text.en: Record the tune of It Came Upon the Midnight Clear in Sing, with the other parts playing.
text.es: Graba la melodía de It Came Upon the Midnight Clear en Cantar, con las demás voces sonando.

text.en: John H. Morison, the editor who received the carol in 1849, later wrote that however poor his own Christmas sermon might be, "the reading and singing of this hymn are enough to make up for all deficiencies".
text.es: John H. Morison, el editor que recibió el villancico en 1849, escribió años después que, por pobre que fuera su propio sermón de Navidad, "la lectura y el canto de este himno bastan para suplir todas las deficiencias".

source.en: Alfred P. Putnam, Singers and Songs of the Liberal Faith (Boston: Roberts Brothers, 1875), "Edmund Hamilton Sears", p. 308, Morison's letter; Princeton Theological Seminary Library copy, read from the scan
source.es: Alfred P. Putnam, Singers and Songs of the Liberal Faith (Boston: Roberts Brothers, 1875), "Edmund Hamilton Sears", p. 308, carta de Morison; ejemplar de la Princeton Theological Seminary Library, leído en el escaneo
